# function: node_name

Builds a node name as `<prefix>-<index>`, with the index zero-padded to at least two digits: `node_name("r", 1)` gives `r-01`, `node_name("r", 12)` gives `r-12` and `node_name("r", 100)` gives `r-100`. Useful with `count.index` or `for_each`. The prefix must not be empty and the index must not be negative.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Provider functions need the provider in required_providers.
terraform {
  required_providers {
    gns3 = {
      source  = "JerryBalmer1/gns3"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-node-name"
}

data "gns3_template" "vpcs" {
  name = "VPCS"
}

# PC-01, PC-02 and PC-03.
resource "gns3_node" "pc" {
  count       = 3
  project_id  = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id = data.gns3_template.vpcs.template_id
  name        = provider::gns3::node_name("PC", count.index + 1)
  x           = count.index * 150
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
node_name(prefix string, index number) string
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `prefix` (String) Text before the dash, such as `r` or `sw`. Must not be empty.
1. `index` (Number) Number after the dash, zero-padded to at least two digits. Must be 0 or more.
